newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI says to buy 26.8 pct of Lonrho.
newsitem.headline: JCI says to buy 26.8 pct of Lonrho.

text.p: JCI Ltd announced on Wednesday it would acquire a 26.8 percent of Lonrho Plc for approximately 2.5 billion rand.

The company said in a statement that in terms of an agreement reached earlier, it had been granted call options on Anglo American Corp, De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd and The Southern Life Association's combined holdings of some 211.08 million Lonrho shares -- effectively a 26.8 percent stake.
In turn, JCI Ltd had granted the three companies put options on their stake in Lonrho. It said it would pay 11.64 rand or 155 pence per share for the stake.
"The options, exerciseable during December 1997, are conditional inter alia upon the approvals of the European Commission and the shareholders of JCI Ltd," it said.
The announcement follows a ruling by the European Comission in April that Anglo American had to reduce its 27.5 percent stake in Lonrho to 9.99 percent to avoid controlling the platinum market.
Subsequent to the ruling, JCI Ltd and Lonrho entered talks on a possible merger between the two groups, but these were called off on Monday.
JCI Ltd then issued a cautionary saying it was dicsussing other ways to unlock value for the two firms' shareholders.
Chairman Mzi Khumalo said the reason the merger talks with Lonrho had been called off was that it had not been comfortable that JCI Ltd's assets were being properly valued in the merger process.
"However, I am confident that many of the synergistic and other benefits which formed the basis of the original proposal, can now be achieved through the conclusion of this deal," Khumalo said.

The company said the deal would provide for close co-operation between JCI and Lonrho and position them to take advantage of the realignment and restructuring currently taking place within the South African mining industry.

"Further, the transaction will provide JCI with a strategic interest in Lonrho's valuable portfolio of international assets and will enable JCI to participate in the expected rerating of Lonrho as Lonrho increases its focus on its mining business," the company said.
Lonrho's prime international asset is its 33.6 percent stake in Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields Company Ltd -- one of the most successful gold producers in Africa.
Anglo American desperately wants a stake in Ashanti and said last week that Lonrho had suggested swapping its stake in Ashanti for Anglo's shares.
JCI said that a further announcement would be made shortly, setting out the financial effects of the transaction.
It advised shareholders to continue exercising caution in their sharedealings until a further announcement was made.
